title: clarify-credential-lifecycle-docstrings-and-typed-stream-examples
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Clarify credential TTL/rotation semantics in SDKs; add example patterns for typed async streams in TypeScript and context-manager style session handling in Python. Minor Go API rename for Receiver -> StreamConsumer to improve parity.

description: Context and motivation: Teams building long-lived streaming integrations have reported confusion about when SDK credentials are refreshed vs. when application code should trigger refresh. Simultaneously, our TypeScript ergonomic examples for typed async streams diverged from Python/Go patterns and caused portability questions. This PR unifies guidance, tightens docstrings, and adds small API ergonomics to reduce footguns. Summary of changes: 1) Python: introduce Session context manager (sdk/python/session.py) that centralizes credential acquisition, TTL semantics, and a lightweight background refresh probe. Docstrings and README were expanded to show three canonical patterns: short-lived interactive requests, long-lived streaming with periodic lease refresh, and delegated-credential fallbacks. Added unit tests (test_session_ttl.py) around TTL edge cases and race conditions. 2) TypeScript: provide a typed async-iterator example (examples/typed-pullstream.ts) that demonstrates backpressure hints, retry-policy combinators (policies.ts), and a recommended shape for consumer code to interoperate with Redwood servers. The example intentionally uses an exported RetryPolicy builder to demonstrate composition (exponential backoff + jitter + max-window). 3) Go: rename internal Receiver interface to StreamConsumer to better reflect cross-language naming; provide a small compatibility shim (consumer.go / receiver_shim.go) so downstream users see a deprecation warning instead of breakage. 4) Docs: unify the credential lifecycle documentation (docs/reference/sdk-auth.md) with explicit TTL definitions, examples of safe refresh windows (e.g. refresh when remaining_ttl < 0.2 * lease_duration), and migration notes (docs/migration/2026-02-sdk-parity.md). 5) Tests & CI: added invariant tests for credential tombstoning, TTL refresh probe, and typed-stream examples run under TS checker. Checklist: - [x] Add Session context manager and tests (Python) - [x] Add typed TS streaming example and RetryPolicy combinators - [x] Add Go rename + shim + tests - [x] Update docs and migration notes - [x] Update changelogs and bump SDK versions (py 0.14.0rc1, ts 2.8.0-rc, go 1.6.0-rc) Compatibility and migration notes: - Python: new Session is opt-in; existing low-level TokenProvider APIs are unchanged. Customers using custom keepalive loops will see no forced behavior, but we recommend adopting Session for shorter code and fewer edgecases. - TypeScript: example introduces a small helper export RetryPolicy.compose(...). This is additive; no user-facing breaking changes. - Go: StreamConsumer rename is exported in the new package and the shim prints a single deprecation log on init. We will remove the shim in the next major version (see migration doc). Review notes and discussion: initial review called out wording in the Python docstrings that implied auto-refresh would be guaranteed; changed docstrings to emphasize "best-effort background probe" and added explicit guidance to handle RefreshError. We also tightened the TS type signatures to avoid any "any" escapes in the examples; Diego suggested using a discriminated union for stream events which we adopted. Tests: CI showed a flaky browser-based TypeScript example run in the first run (spurious network timing) causing a transient failure; I added a deterministic mock harness and re-ran. All CI checks are green now. Rollout plan: merge to main behind SDK feature flags for rc releases; publish Python rc to test PyPI, TS rc to npm under tag next, Go rc to a pre-release module path. Follow-ups: - Backport small shim to 0.13.x patch if there are enterprise requests - Add an observability example showing token rotation traces in Redwood Console - Consider adding an opt-in lease-refresh metric in SDK surface for Dedicated customers Review conversation (high level): - Diego Morales: "Nit: change 'refresh window' example to be 20% of lease not 10% — otherwise clients will hit refresh storms." -> Changed and added safety jitter. - Priya Patel: "Can we avoid global goroutines in the Go shim? They can complicate server-side lifecycles." -> Reworked shim to use OnNewStream lifecycle hook. - Liam O'Connor: "Please call out that RefreshError should not be retried indefinitely; include recommended backoff in docs." -> Added RetryPolicy recipe and unit tests. Merge outcome: squash-merged after approvals from Diego and Priya. CI green at merge time.
